name: Sticky Rice Cakes (Kholak)
instructions: 1. Soak the glutinous rice in water for at least 4 to 6 hours or overnight.
2. Drain the water and steam the rice until it is fully cooked and translucent.
3. Transfer the hot cooked rice into a wooden mortar and pound it using a pestle until it turns into a thick, sticky, uniform dough-like consistency.
4. Add a pinch of salt if desired during the pounding process.
5. Grease your hands with a little water or oil, take small portions of the sticky rice, and shape them into round or oval cakes.
6. Optionally, wrap the cakes in clean banana leaves to impart flavor and keep them moist.
7. Serve warm, either as is or lightly toasted over a flame.
description: Kholak is a quintessential Naga snack showcasing the community's reliance on locally grown sticky rice. It is a simple yet essential food item, often carried by farmers or travelers as a portable, energy-dense meal that reflects the indigenous culinary practices of the Naga tribes.
